estimates.notes: This paragraph reports expert-rated objective creativity despite appearing under the Self-reported creativity heading. The printed t and d have the human-minus-LLM orientation, opposite to the treatment/control order of this record; signs are preserved without recalculation. The paper does not name the standardizer for d or identify the estimand of the confidence interval. The interval is retained with ci_of=null and is not assigned to d or to a raw difference. The separate one-way and factorial ANOVA records are alternative analyses of this same outcome and sample, not independent effects. Arm counts are unreported in the saved article.

open_items: The external supplement is not saved with this article and could not be retrieved in this job. Supplementary Tables S5–S6 may print arm counts; Tables S7–S8 may print further regression results. Supplementary coverage remains unverified.

Randomized and analyzed counts by partner/response arm are absent from the saved article. No equal-allocation counts have been inferred from the total, degrees of freedom or external data-inspection notes.

The estimand of the Experiment 1 confidence interval is unidentified. Its endpoints do not contain the reported d; ci_of remains null. The d standardizer is also unspecified, and the printed signs follow the human-minus-LLM ordering.

Experiment 2 does not print full-sample creativity means, dispersions, a signed treatment difference or a signed standardized effect. Its F test and partial eta squared alone do not establish the direction of the pooled contrast.
Overlap between participants in the two experiments is not stated. No combined unique-person total is inferred, and demographic differences do not establish independent samples.
The paper does not identify the participant recruitment country, the specific ERNIE Bot model version or its release year. Recruitment was paid and online, but a panel provider is not named.
No preregistration or preregistered primary outcome is stated in the saved article.

Excluded task-specific results have unresolved printed dispersion labels, and the Experiment 1 complex-task F/P combination is inconsistent. These should be checked against the supplement or authors if task-specific effects are later brought into scope.

The fixation measure’s reference idea set in the human-partner condition is not explained, and the Experiment 2 moderated-mediation index conflicts with its verbal interpretation. These concerns affect excluded mechanism results.
notes: Extracted on 2026-10-09 from the saved PDF and the entire markdown conversion, including all references and end matter. The PDF has no appended or embedded supplement. Figures were inspected, and cited pages were checked with PyMuPDF; mathematical symbols in quotes were transcribed from the rendered PDF where the text layer had broken encodings. The full-sample statistic inventory is preserved in separate rows: the Experiment 1 pooled t-test and d with arm means and SDs and an unidentified confidence interval; the matching one-way ANOVA and partial eta squared; the factorial partner main effect and partial eta squared; and the Experiment 2 factorial response-type main effect and partial eta squared. The Experiment 1 rows are alternative analyses of one contrast and must not be counted as independent effects. Task complexity is explicitly the paper’s moderator. Conditional simple effects within task-complexity levels are excluded under the extraction specification’s full-sample and no-moderation rules, even though the screening form lists those randomized factorial cells as arms. Only supplied-file evidence is used for numerical extraction. Requests to the paper’s DOI supplementary destination and the named OSF API were attempted using urllib with the required User-Agent; both failed with a local socket-permission error, so neither source was inspected remotely. The separate data-availability form describes raw participant data, but its computed row counts and summaries were not imported as printed paper statistics. No quantities were computed, signs reversed, confidence-interval estimands guessed, or figure heights digitized. The online_panel population code follows the screening form; the actual recruitment channel is unspecified. The broad idea_generation task code includes the alternative-uses and product-feature tasks pooled in these full-sample analyses. No across-people diversity or post-assistance outcome is reported.
